jobs.title: Sr Director, Corporate Strategy & Projects
jobs.description:
At Gilead, we’re creating a healthier world for all people. For more than 35 years, we’ve tackled diseases such as HIV, viral hepatitis, COVID-19 and cancer – working relentlessly to develop therapies that help improve lives and to ensure access to these therapies across the globe. We continue to fight against the world’s biggest health challenges, and our mission requires collaboration, determination and a relentless drive to make a difference.

Every member of Gilead’s team plays a critical role in the discovery and development of life-changing scientific innovations. Our employees are our greatest asset as we work to achieve our bold ambitions, and we’re looking for the next wave of passionate and ambitious people ready to make a direct impact.

We believe every employee deserves a great leader. People Leaders are the cornerstone to the employee experience at Gilead and Kite. As a people leader now or in the future, you are the key driver in evolving our culture and creating an environment where every employee feels included, developed and empowered to fulfil their aspirations. Join Gilead and help create possible, together.

Job Description

Reporting to the VP, Corporate Strategy & Projects, the Senior Director serves as a strategic thought partner to senior leadership, helping shape enterprise strategy, influencing critical decisions, and leading initiatives that drive long-term value creation.

This leader identifies, frames, and advances the company's most important strategic decisions, translating long-term ambition into actionable priorities and measurable outcomes. The Senior Director builds alignment across senior leaders, influences enterprise decision-making, and drives complex initiatives requiring executive sponsorship and broad organizational engagement.

Success in this role requires building trusted partnerships across the enterprise. Team members are expected to have exceptional strategic judgment, executive presence, influence, and the ability to connect perspectives across functions to drive enterprise outcomes.

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Enterprise Strategy & Insights

- - Serve as a strategic advisor to the VP and senior leaders on high-priority enterprise issues.
- Lead development of strategic frameworks, recommendations, and perspectives on the company's most critical business challenges.
- Lead major components of corporate strategy development, enterprise planning, and scenario planning.
- Assess external trends, strategic risks, and long-term growth opportunities to help shape enterprise priorities and strategic direction.

- Strategic Initiatives & Execution

- - Own and independently lead complex enterprise initiatives sponsored by executive leadership.
- Establish governance structures and operating mechanisms that enable effective execution and decision-making.
- Drive enterprise outcomes by aligning stakeholders, resolving competing priorities, and ensuring delivery against strategic objectives.

- Cross-Functional Leadership & Influence

- - Align leaders across functions around enterprise priorities and strategic decisions.
- Lead cross-functional problem solving and influence decisions in highly matrixed environments.
- Foster enterprise-first thinking, collaboration, and high-quality decision-making.

- Executive & Board Engagement

- - Lead development of strategic recommendations and executive communications for senior leadership and the Board.
- Shape Board and GLT discussions through strategic insights, recommendations, and facilitation of workshops, strategy sessions, and other key forums.
- Serve as a trusted advisor on enterprise strategic matters.

- Organizational & Talent Development

- - Contribute to a culture of curiosity, collaboration, and continuous improvement
- Mentor and coach junior team members and rotational talent.
- Foster an enterprise mindset and strategic leadership capabilities across the organization.

Basic Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree and 14+ years of relevant experience; or Master's degree, MBA, PhD, or MD and 12+ years of relevant experience.
- Significant experience in corporate strategy, management consulting, corporate development, business operations, finance, or related fields.
- Strong understanding of Gilead's portfolio, business model, and strategic context.

Preferred Qualifications
- Deep biotechnology, biopharmaceutical, or life sciences expertise.
- Demonstrated success influencing enterprise-level strategic decisions.
- Proven experience leading large-scale cross-functional strategic initiatives.
- Experience developing corporate or enterprise strategy.
- Experience partnering directly with executive leadership and supporting Board-level discussions.
- Strong systems-thinking orientation and enterprise mindset.
- Ability to balance long-term strategic thinking with executional pragmatism.
- Executive presence and confidence challenging assumptions constructively.
- Exceptional communication, stakeholder management, and influence skills.
- Expertise in executive storytelling and strategic communications.
- Proven ability to develop and mentor high-potential talent.
- Ability to thrive in highly ambiguous and rapidly evolving environments.

The salary range for this position is: $261,375.00 - $338,250.00. Gilead considers a variety of factors when determining base compensation, including experience, qualifications, and geographic location. These considerations mean actual compensation will vary. This position may also be eligible for a discretionary annual bonus, discretionary stock-based long-term incentives (eligibility may vary based on role), paid time off, and a benefits package. Reporting to the VP, Corporate Strategy & Projects, the Executive Director is accountable for leading defined components of Gilead’s enterprise strategy agenda and owning a portfolio of the company’s highest-priority strategic initiatives. This leader drives assigned strategic questions from framing to decision, developing fact-based options, trade-offs, and recommendations while partnering closely with the VP, Gilead Leadership Team, and senior leaders to shape enterprise direction and strategic choices.

- Demonstrated success owning major components of corporate, portfolio, or business-unit strategy.

- Exceptional ability to frame ambiguous strategic questions and develop rigorous options, trade-offs, and recommendations.
- Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders, challenge assumptions constructively, and generate alignment without formal authority.

jobs.title: Associate Director, Operations Oversight Lead Medical Affairs Research Global Operations (MARGO)
jobs.description:
At Gilead, we’re creating a healthier world for all people. For more than 35 years, we’ve tackled diseases such as HIV, viral hepatitis, COVID-19 and cancer – working relentlessly to develop therapies that help improve lives and to ensure access to these therapies across the globe. We continue to fight against the world’s biggest health challenges, and our mission requires collaboration, determination and a relentless drive to make a difference.

Every member of Gilead’s team plays a critical role in the discovery and development of life-changing scientific innovations. Our employees are our greatest asset as we work to achieve our bold ambitions, and we’re looking for the next wave of passionate and ambitious people ready to make a direct impact.

We believe every employee deserves a great leader. People Leaders are the cornerstone to the employee experience at Gilead and Kite. As a people leader now or in the future, you are the key driver in evolving our culture and creating an environment where every employee feels included, developed and empowered to fulfil their aspirations. Join Gilead and help create possible, together.

Job Description

MARGO Background:
The MARGO function is part of the wider Medical Affairs Research (MAR) department within the Development organization and operationalises Non Interventional Studies scientifically led from MAR. MAR conducts observational research and generates analysis results to inform decisions throughout the product lifecycle across research, development, post-approval, and commercialization. Observational research is conducted on data collected from individuals assessed for biomedical, health and other outcomes, and includes observational studies and observational analyses. Source data for observational studies may be based on primary data
collection, secondary data use, or both. The study results, generated using a rigorous process, provide insights and evidence for internal (e.g., program, safety) and external (e.g., regulators, healthcare providers) stakeholders.
Position Summary:
This role provides end-to-end operational oversight of observational studies within the MAR portfolio across all therapeutic areas (TA). This position supports the MAR team in high-quality, compliant and timely study execution of the study portfolio through effective vendor oversight, risk management and issue resolution. This role reports to the Director, MAARGO and is the primary point of contact for study operations for vendors and service providers. While not responsible for day-to-day execution, the role is responsible for collaborating with MAR scientific leads, Quality, Clinical Operations, Regulatory Affairs, Medical Affairs and other stakeholders to ensure vendors and service providers meet agreed-upon timelines and are compliant with process requirements and relevant regulatory guidelines.

Key Responsibilities:
• Responsible for working with the MARGO Leadership Team to track, prioritize and manage the execution of observational studies across all TA portfolios
• Collaborate with MARGO Leadership Team on strategic sourcing options to optimize the execution of the TA portfolio
• Responsible for vendor performance management, issue management and escalation of risks impacting the portfolio
• Responsible for the vendor oversight plans, and performance and quality checks of study deliverables per the vendor oversight process
• Partner with vendor outsourcing to support initiation and execution of study vendor and service provider agreements
• Collaborate with MAR scientific leads to ensure alignment of study objectives and timelines across all stakeholders and vendors
• Own end-to-end oversight of study deliverables, ensuring timely, high-quality completion aligned to TA priorities, with proactive risk identification and mitigation
• Track study milestones, timelines, deliverables and financials; proactively identify and mitigate risks
• Collaborate with MAR scientific leads to monitor utilization and assignment of resources to deliver on priorities established by the MARGO Leadership Team
• Ensure onboarding of study vendors and service provider resources to support the study portfolio priorities established with the MARGO Leadership Team
• Monitor end-to-end processes to ensure compliance with process requirements, regulatory guidelines and study objectives
• Serve as an escalation point to resolve quality, scope and timeliness issues with operational stakeholders, including vendors and service providers
• Maintain regular communication with operational stakeholders, study vendors and service providers to ensure delivery against priorities and commitments
• Identify opportunities for process improvement, increased standardization and operational efficiency
• Collaborate with other oversight roles within MAR to drive consistency across study execution processes and implement best practices
• Liaison with Quality on periodic quality reviews and other quality related activities
• Escalate study specific issues to Quality for guidance and consultation

Qualifications:
• Previous experience in study operations or project management providing operational and financial oversight of observational studies
• BS degree in Biology, Business, Operations Research or equivalent
• Hands-on training and experience in managing study lifecycles in GxP compliant environment
• Demonstrated experience in managing cross-functional study teams and vendor resources to balance priorities and timelines in a matrixed environment
• Proven ability to communicate the scope, requirements, expectations and standards for executing observational studies
• Proven track record of assessing vendor proposals e.g., timelines, deliverables and budget to meet study objectives
• Demonstrated vendor management experience to conduct primary data collection and secondary data use studies
• Demonstrated ability to collaborate cross-functionally with program, study and functional teams, and vendor resources
• Knowledge of global NIS regulatory landscape
• Experience in working with international entities to conduct observational studies
• Ability to work collaboratively with global cross-functional stakeholders
• Ability to communicate study requirements and results
• Strong problem-solving skills using data driven approaches
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills

We are pleased to share that Gilead’s Stockley Park and Holborn offices are planning to come together at a new London headquarters at 1 Triton Square, NW1, from approximately Q2 2027. Applicants should consider this planned location change when applying for this role. Gilead operates a flexible working policy, offering a balanced approach with two days of remote working and three days working onsite.

jobs.title: Director, Business Strategy and Operations
jobs.description:
We’re here for one reason and one reason only – to cure cancer. Every moment is dedicated to developing treatments and every action moves us one step closer to our goal. We’ve made incredible scientific breakthroughs and our pioneering personalized CAR T-cell therapies have changed the paradigm. But we're not finished yet.

Join Kite, as we make even bigger advances in cancer therapies, and help shape where our business and medical science goes next.

We believe every employee deserves a great leader. People Leaders are the cornerstone to the employee experience at Gilead and Kite. As a people leader now or in the future, you are the key driver in evolving our culture and creating an environment where every employee feels included, developed and empowered to fulfil their aspirations. Join Kite and help create more tomorrows.

Job Description

The Director, Business Strategy & Operations reports to the Vice President and General Manager, US Commercial, and serves as a strategic and operational partner focused on improving organizational effectiveness and business impact. The role leads business strategy, planning, operating cadence, executive decision support, and organizational effectiveness, partnering across US Commercial to translate priorities into coordinated action and measurable outcomes. This role is based at Kite’s Santa Monica, California, headquarters.

Kite is transitioning from its current Santa Monica headquarters, with employees expected to relocate to our El Segundo, CA or Thousand Oaks, CA office beginning in January 2027. While this role will be based in Santa Monica through 2026, applicants should take this planned relocation into consideration. Kite supports a flexible working policy, offering a balanced approach with two days of remote working and three days working onsite.

This position can be based out of El Segundo, CA, Thousand Oaks, CA or Foster City, CA.

Key Responsibilities
- Serve as a trusted advisor to the General Manager (GM), synthesizing complex information into executive-ready insights, recommendations, decision materials, and Board-level communications.
- Translate strategy into priorities, roadmaps, performance measures, operating rhythms, and actionable plans, driving strategic initiatives from development through execution.
- Lead annual strategic, financial, resource, and headcount planning, including coordination of the consolidated Plan of Action.
- Design and manage leadership governance, planning cycles, quarterly business reviews, and accountability mechanisms that enable timely decisions and disciplined execution.
- Coordinate enterprise and functional initiatives across US Commercial, aligning ownership, resources, dependencies, risks, sequencing, and measures of success.
- Represent US Commercial in enterprise and global planning forums, shaping broader decisions and translating enterprise direction into clear commitments for the US business.
- Track business performance and commitments, identify barriers, and drive mitigation, course correction, productivity, and process improvements.
- Lead planning and execution for major GM-sponsored meetings, including National and Midyear Meetings.
- Partner with commercial leadership to coordinate cross-functional readiness for anticipated US product launches.
- Advance organizational and leadership effectiveness by improving how the organization operates, collaborates, communicates, and makes decisions.
- Develop high-impact communications for leadership meetings, business reviews, all-hands presentations, and internal and external audiences.
- Serve on the Kite Commercial BS&O Forum, ensuring alignment between Commercial Strategy & Operations priorities and US Commercial planning and execution.

Basic Qualifications
Advanced scientific degree (i.e., MD, PharmD, PhD) and 8+ years of experience OR
Master’s Degree and 10+ years of experience
OR
Bachelor’s Degree and 12+ years of experience

Preferred Qualifications
- Significant pharmaceutical or biopharmaceutical experience leading complex strategic and operational initiatives; experience in commercial, finance, or consulting is preferred.
- Ability to translate enterprise strategy into practical plans and deliver results with rigor, accountability, and attention to detail.
- Strong executive presence, judgment, communication, and stakeholder-influence skills, including the ability to lead without direct authority.
- Demonstrated enterprise mindset and ability to navigate ambiguity, connect cross-functional priorities, and manage competing trade-offs.
- Experience with business planning, financial and resource analysis, project management, and product profit-and-loss considerations.
- Proactive, adaptable, and resourceful, with strong emotional intelligence, curiosity, and a continuous-improvement mindset.
- Demonstrated experience driving organizational transformation and operating model effectiveness, including leading change management and adoption across complex, matrixed environments.

People Leader Accountabilities :

- Create Inclusion - knowing the business value of diverse teams, modeling inclusion, and embedding the value of diversity in the way they manage their teams.

- Extensive ERP experience as a user and business process owner, including familiarity with typical transactions and master data configuration.

- Deep understanding of cGMP clinical and commercial manufacturing operations, planning, supply chain, and regulatory requirements.

- Excellent business acumen, organizational and communication (both written and verbal) skills.

- Proven ability to lead complex, global transformation initiatives, influence stakeholders without authority, manage ambiguity, and drive adoption through effective communication and change leadership.

- Strategic thinking and ability to constructively challenge the status quo.

- Ability to manage multiple priorities, to draw out diverse views, and to effectively manage challenging conversations with tact and empathy.

For more than 35 years, we’ve tackled diseases such as HIV, viral hepatitis, COVID-19 and cancer – working relentlessly to develop therapies that help improve lives and to ensure access to these therapies across the globe. We continue to fight against the world’s biggest health challenges, and our mission requires collaboration, determination and a relentless drive to make a difference.

Every member of Gilead’s team plays a critical role in the discovery and development of life-changing scientific innovations. Our employees are our greatest asset as we work to achieve our bold ambitions, and we’re looking for the next wave of passionate and ambitious people ready to make a direct impact.

We believe every employee deserves a great leader. People Leaders are the cornerstone to the employee experience at Gilead and Kite. As a people leader now or in the future, you are the key driver in evolving our culture and creating an environment where every employee feels included, developed and empowered to fulfil their aspirations. Join Gilead and help create possible, together.

Job Description

Intern - Human Resources - Strategy & Operations

As a Gilead intern you will contribute to high-impact meaningful projects that will not only further advance our company’s mission but will allow you to gain real world experience at one of the most innovative organizations in the world.  You will also have opportunities to participate in special events including professional development and leadership presentations, social/network building activities and local community volunteer programs.

Key Responsibilities will include, but are not limited to the following:
- Perform all assigned tasks accurately, efficiently and in accordance with applicable policies and procedures

- Work closely with members of assigned team to develop subject matter knowledge

- Attend company/department/team trainings and meetings as appropriate

- Maintain accurate and updated employee records in accordance with company policies and government regulations

- Provide answers to employee questions and problem-solves as needed

- Assist in the development and improvement of HR processes and procedures

- Compose competent employee communications regarding HR information and process changes

- Prepare HR-related reports and surveys

- Showcase your work with a final presentation (PPT) near the conclusion of your internship

Required Qualifications:
- Must be at least 18 years of age at the start of the internship.

- Must be enrolled full‑time in a Bachelor’s, Master’s, MBA, JD or PhD program at a nationally accredited U.S. college or university, with continued full‑time enrollment required in the Fall semester following the internship.

- Must be currently enrolled as an undergraduate (freshman, sophomore, junior, or senior) or as a graduate/doctoral student.

- Must have a minimum overall cumulative GPA of 2.8 at the time of application and hire (official transcripts will be requested).

- Must be independently authorized to work in the United States now and in the future (current or future work authorization must not require school or employer sponsorship) official transcripts are required.

- Must be able to commit to a full‑time internship lasting 10–12 consecutive weeks between May and August.

- Must be willing and able to work at the designated site for the duration of the internship (relocation may be required). All internships are hybrid; fully remote roles are not offered.

Preferred Qualifications :
- Preferred degree level: Undergraduate, Graduate, MBA, PhD, JD, or PharmD (based on role alignment)

- Proficiency with Microsoft Office (MS Office) tools, such as Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook

- Strong problem‑solving skills, with the ability to identify issues and proactively seek solutions

- Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team in a collaborative environment

- Demonstrated commitment to inclusion and diversity, including the ability to work respectfully with individuals from diverse backgrounds

- Highly organized, detail‑oriented, and able to manage competing priorities in a fast‑paced environment with short timelines

Gilead Core Values:
- Integrity (Doing What’s Right)

- Inclusion (Encouraging Diversity)

- Teamwork (Working Together)

- Excellence (Being Your Best)

- Accountability (Taking Personal Responsibility)

The expected hourly range for this position is $20.00 - $55.00.

Job Description

JOB RESPONSIBILITIES
- serves as a key strategic partner to the Vice President of Operations and the Site Leadership Team, enabling the La Verne site to achieve its short- and long-term business objectives through strong strategy deployment, operational discipline, organizational change management, communication, digital enablement, and operational excellence.
- This role is accountable for translating site, PDM, and enterprise priorities into actionable plans, governance routines, performance management systems, and cross-functional execution mechanisms.
- The position provides leadership across multiple strategic and operational workstreams and ensures alignment between business priorities, resources, organizational capability, and site performance.
- Ultimate responsibility for staff development, budgeting and cost control, and multi-function strategic planning.
- Models strong leadership, accountable for talent mapping, succession planning and the development of strong leaders within the function.
- Provides leadership to direct reports and builds a highly capable team through the attraction, training and development of the necessary skilled professionals to meet business needs.
- Inspires culture and institutes key processes necessary to achieve long and short-term strategic goals.
- Anticipates shifts in industry trends and regulatory environment that will impact Gilead’s business needs and positions the function to respond accordingly.
- Ensures that departments operate in accordance with department SOPs which meet regulatory and GMP standards.
- Establishes and publishes Key Performance Indicators.

Strategy Development and Implementation
- Act as key strategic advisor, leading the development and execution of short- and long-range strategic plans in alignment with PDM strategy and ambition, company goals, market trends and in partnership with Site Leadership Team (SLT).
- Provides insight in developing, prioritization and communicating site-wide priorities and initiatives. Creates buy-in for the business plans and vision for the future to ensure goals and operating budgets are aligned and achieved.
- Institutes key processes necessary to achieve long and short-term goals.
- Develop plans to translate strategic objectives into tactical implementation of new technologies and processes to enhance production efficiency.
- Serves as a key business partner to senior management team focusing on strategic issues across multiple functions.
- Monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) to track progress and identify areas for further optimization.
- Build strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders to facilitate collaboration and alignment on strategic and operational priorities.
- Coordination of the SLT in support of the VP of operations.
- Support the development of a culture that aligns with the company values, encouraging growth and learning mindset while ensuring accountability and retaining key talent in a positive environment.

Organization Change Management & Communication
- Lead the organizational change management strategy for major site initiatives, ensuring business changes are effectively planned, communicated, adopted, and sustained.
- Communicate manufacturing site strategy and progress to senior management, including regular updates on performance metrics.
- Partner with the VP of Operations, SLT, HR, Communications, and functional leaders to ensure messaging is aligned, timely, transparent, and connected to site values and strategic pillars.
- Lead the “organizational change management” of the site by developing communication plans and ensure effective communication strategies are in place within the organization, including two-way communication channels.
- Accountable for the success of formal organizational change management impacting all business units.
- Strengthen site-wide change readiness by building leader capability in communication, stakeholder engagement, and change adoption.
- Support leaders in translating complex business changes into practical, audience-specific messages that promote understanding, engagement, and ownership.

Operational Excellence
- Champion continuous improvement methodologies and establish sustainable processes that improve productivity and effectiveness.
- Develop and lead the La Verne operational excellence strategy in alignment with site priorities, business needs, quality expectations, and enterprise goals.
- Manages multiple cross-functional projects.
- Conduct process analysis, identify bottlenecks and inefficiencies, and design and implement process improvement solutions using methodologies like Lean Six Sigma, or other continuous improvement frameworks.
- Identify cost-saving opportunities within the manufacturing process including materials, labor, and overhead expenses.
- Leads the organizational change management process, including communication, training, and stakeholder engagement to ensure successful adoption of new processes.
- Utilize data analytics to measure performance, identify trends, and track progress on improvement initiatives.
- Build and manage a high-performing team of operational excellence professionals, providing coaching and development opportunities.
- Work closely with cross-functional teams across departments to identify and implement operational improvements.
- Foster a culture of continuous improvement, encouraging employee engagement and feedback on process improvement opportunities.
- Ensure operational excellence initiatives are supported by appropriate change management, communication, training, adoption, and sustainment plans.

BS Degree and 14 years - or
Master's Degree and 12 years - or
PhD and Twelve years

Job Description

The Oncology Business, Strategy, and Operations Lead will play a pivotal role in supporting the SVP of Oncology Clinical Development in building and executing the strategic vision for the Oncology Therapeutic Area (TA). As Gilead Oncology enters an exciting phase of growth and investment, this position offers the unique opportunity to collaborate directly with senior leadership to advance a world-class clinical development team, build the portfolio, and elevate oncology as a key focus area for Gilead.

RESPONSIBILITIES
- As a member of the Oncology Leadership Team  help to design and facilitate Leadership team meetings, drive team engagement planning and execution, participate in decision making and strategy development, support the team’s overall success.

- Business Strategy : A strategic advisor who provides trusted input and helps test ideas, especially for the oncology portfolio from research through launch. This role is a thought partner, facilitating strategic projects and enabling execution of the business strategy.
- Collaboration with Corporate Development: Aligns oncology strategy with program and asset acquisitions, overseeing diligence staffing and evaluation.

- Key contributor in staffing and resource allocation:   Liaise across Franchise Heads and HR to ensure the right talent and opportunities align with strategic priorities.
- Goals & KPI’s : supports the leader and leadership team to define short and longer term goals and defining objectives and KPI’s for the TA, ensuring interconnectivity at a functional and enterprise level.
- Special Projects : May lead or participate in initiatives in support of strategic priorities in support of anything from strategy to execution or growth.
- Business Operations : maintain a comprehensive view of the priorities, projects, decisions, and actions that supports the Executive and tracks business area goals, study and functional budgets and growth.
- Effectively network across the organization  and communicate with cross functional leaders to connect projects and workstreams that would otherwise remain siloed.  This includes key collaboration with Kite as part of the oncology strategy and portfolio
- Serve as a key business partner   and conduit  to the leader ensuring that work within the team flows smoothly by driving operational efficiency and effectiveness, strategic alignment and integration of activities
- Acts as an amplifier for their leader ; will prepare and deliver presentations, manage existing communications strategies, and innovate new ones.

CAPABILITIES & REQUIREMENTS
- Super Organizer  — able to stay personally organized while managing the priorities of the executive. Able to help bring order and effectively manage complex and ambiguous projects
- Collaborative, empathetic  —assist in building the networked organization— tearing down walls and silos so teams communicate better while maintaining a constant eye on how the teams feel.
- Sense of Urgency  —self-starter acts with an entrepreneurial spirit promoting a bias towards action and speed of execution on the team.
- High EQ  — displays humility and adopts a mature approach to feedback and open to learning from any member of the team and other key stakeholders.
- Highly Persuasive  - has strong interpersonal and communication skills with a demonstrated ability to present at an executive level.  Knows how to get things done across a complex matrix and able to influence without direct authority.
- Strategic Thinker  —able to see the big picture of things.  A strategic, enterprise mindset helps align detailed work to the overall strategy, as well as evaluate what is urgent versus important.
- Strong Reputation — for getting things done and never dropping the ball.  The EVP and the leadership team need to know that responsibilities and tasks that fall to the Chief of Staff are guaranteed to get done.
- Trusted Operator  — able to work with and manage the dissemination of sensitive and confidential information with the utmost discretion.
- Expert Facilitator  — Finally, a day-to-day part of the role requires managing conversations, synthesizing multiple points of view, and aligning on direction…all in an impartial and professional way.
- Strong Communication - has good communication skills across different mediums, is able to influence and connect with key stakeholders and use those communication skills to move work forward.

- Organizational Excellence : Maintains personal organization while managing complex, ambiguous projects and executive priorities.
- Collaborative & Empathetic : Promotes a networked organization by breaking down silos, fostering strong team communication, and being attentive to team dynamics.
- Results-Oriented & Proactive : Demonstrates a strong sense of urgency, acting with an entrepreneurial mindset to drive action and ensure timely execution.
- Strategic Influence : Possesses high emotional intelligence, strong interpersonal and communication skills, and effectively influences across a complex matrix without direct authority.
- Trusted & Reliable : Known for discretion with confidential matters and a reputation for follow-through, ensuring leadership can depend on deliverables being met.
- Expert Facilitator & Communicator : Synthesizes diverse perspectives, aligns on direction impartially, and communicates effectively with stakeholders to advance workstreams.

Competencies
- Enterprise and Functional Mindset :  Aligns priorities and projects to the broader organizational vision and strategy. Uses peripheral vision instead of focusing only on what is in front of them.
- Adaptability:   Adopts a positive approach when faced with change, complexity and uncertainty and able to adjusts thinking and approach based on new information or events.
- Results Orientation:  Demonstrates a determined and committed approach to achieving results and follows tasks and projects through to completion
- Strategic Planning:  Formulates clear, practical approaches to help meet strategic objectives; anticipates future issues and adapts plans accordingly
- Systemic Thinking:  Recognizes interdependencies of different elements of a process and identifies opportunities to make improvements to processes and systems
- Political Savvy : Understands political issues and knows how to get things done; identifies and successfully influences key decision makers
- Thought Partner:  Asks powerful questions and evaluates new ideas thoroughly. Shares ideas and experiences to help navigate complex challenges
- Business Acumen:  Understands risks/opportunities and uses analytical skills to interpret, translate and simplify complexity to others. Provides analyses, explores a range of solutions and makes recommendations to drive business growth.

Basic Qualifications:
Bachelor's Degree and Fourteen Years' Experience
OR
Masters' Degree and Twelve Years' Experience
OR
PhD and Twelve Years' Experience

Preferred Qualifications:
- PhD, MD in relevant field
- 10+ years in industry drug development, a majority of experience in oncology highly preferred
- Clinical Science and clinical trial experience in development at a large pharma, all phases of development (Ph I-Ph III and filing)
- Strong track record in leadership roles, organizing teams and departments

People Leader Accountabilities:
- Create Inclusion - knowing the business value of diverse teams, modeling inclusion, and embedding the value of diversity in the way they manage their teams.

- Develop Talent - understand the skills, experience, aspirations and potential of their employees and coach them on current performance and future potential. They ensure employees are receiving the feedback and insight needed to grow, develop and realize their purpose.

- Empower Teams - connect the team to the organization by aligning goals, purpose, and organizational objectives, and holding them to account. They provide the support needed to remove barriers and connect their team to the broader ecosystem.

jobs.description:

Job Description

The Director will serve an important role in developing, networking, and executing global strategies that expand and advance the company's ability to deliver robust, competitive technologies in drug delivery and combination products across Gilead’s pharmaceutical asset pipeline and portfolio. This role will serve as a critical bridge between Drug Delivery and Commercial, Medical, and Pharmaceutical Development & Manufacturing (PDM) and related strategy teams. Using strong business acumen and foundational technical expertise, the successful candidate will work collaboratively with cross-functional product teams to identify drug delivery system options and help shape the product system strategy. The candidate will also work across organizational boundaries to identify opportunities for differentiated product-system solutions and develop business cases to help drive strategic investment decisions in the most promising solutions. Through this multi-faceted role, this individual will help to ensure a seamless continuum from commercial strategy to the front-end innovation pipeline, and on to product development and commercialization.

Specific Job Responsibilities
- As a member of the Devices, Packaging, & Process (DPP) organization, contribute to building strategic thought partnerships across Commercial, Marketing, Medical, Global Value & Access, Program Strategy Teams, the broader DPP organization, and other PDM functions to influence program strategy decisions and advance holistic, competitive product-system solutions.

- Serve as the DPP representative on early-stage (pre-pivotal) PDM programs.  In this role, advise on and shape product system strategy and Target Product Profile (TPP) development, ensuring early product system decisions are grounded in patient, market, technical and execution considerations.

- While this position has no direct reports, you will lead teams of scientists, engineers and project managers through dotted lines, to lead scenario planning and business case development for PDM and Gilead Asset Team decision-making, translating technical, commercial, user, and operational inputs into clear product system options and recommendations.

- Monitor the development pipeline and maintain an evolving product roadmap and forecast for DPP across therapeutic areas, linking near-term asset needs with long-term innovation and launch readiness.

- Monitor commercial launches, lifecycle management needs, competitive intelligence, and market/user preference research to generate insights and inform product system strategy and recommendations for PDM program teams and the Device Innovation team.

- Partner closely with Human Factors Engineering, as well as other DPP functions, to identify critical unmet user needs across all therapeutic areas where innovation in product system design can delight and enhance the user experience.

Knowledge & Skills
- Strong business acumen with sufficient technical depth in science, engineering, drug delivery, and/or combination product development to translate complex inputs into practical product-system recommendations.
- Self-motivated, organized, creative, open-minded, patient-focused, results-oriented, and able to demonstrate high learning agility in ambiguous early-stage asset environments.
- Proven ability to lead through dotted lines, build trust-based cross-functional relationships, and influence decisions across Commercial, Medical, PDM, DPP, and leadership stakeholders.
- Strong verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills, including the ability to synthesize technical, market, user, and operational inputs into concise decision-ready recommendations.

- Working knowledge of FDA, EMA, and cGMP standards for combination products.

Required Education & Experience
- Master’s Degree in business, science, or engineering and a minimum of ten (10) years of relevant industry experience; alternatively, a Bachelor’s Degree in science or engineering with a minimum of twelve (12) years of relevant industry experience.
- Preferred: Master’s Degree in business, science, or engineering. Sufficient experience in business-centric roles may be considered in lieu of a business degree.
- Preferred: Demonstrated experience in innovation, development, or commercialization of combination devices or product-system solutions from both technical and strategic perspectives.

People Leader Accountabilities:
- Create Inclusion - knowing the business value of diverse teams, modeling inclusion, and embedding the value of diversity in the way they manage their teams.
- Develop Talent - understand the skills, experience, aspirations and potential of their employees and coach them on current performance and future potential. They ensure employees are receiving the feedback and insight needed to grow, develop and realize their purpose.
- Empower Teams - connect the team to the organization by aligning goals, purpose, and organizational objectives, and holding them to account. They provide the support needed to remove barriers and connect their team to the broader ecosystem.

Reporting into the Corporate & Enterprise Communications team, this role will serve as a strategic communications lead for enterprise transformation work, including operating model evolution, organizational change, new ways of working, capability building, digital and AI-enabled transformation, global capability expansion and other cross-functional initiatives that require clear, coordinated and credible communications.

The Director will partner closely with Public Affairs, Human Resources, Information Technology, Finance, Legal, Compliance, business functions and transformation teams to translate complex business and organizational change into clear, people-centered communications that build trust, reduce confusion and enable engagement. This role requires a strategic thinker and hands-on communicator who can operate across a matrixed global organization, advise senior leaders and help connect transformation priorities into one enterprise narrative.

Enterprise Transformation Strategy & Narrative
- Develop and execute communications strategies that support enterprise transformation priorities, milestones and long-term change journeys.

- Create clear narratives that connect transformation work to business outcomes, employee experience, operational effectiveness, culture and patient impact.

- Maintain consistent messaging across workstreams, audiences, channels, leadership teams and enterprise forums.

- Translate complex operating model, process, technology and organizational changes into accessible communications for broad employee and leader audiences.

- Identify opportunities to connect individual transformation efforts into a broader enterprise story that helps employees see how the work fits together.

Executive Communications & Strategic Advisory
- Serve as a strategic communications advisor to senior leaders sponsoring or leading enterprise transformation initiatives.

- Develop executive presentations, talking points, leader messages, FAQs, cascade materials, town hall content and other leader-ready communications.

- Support communications for leadership forums, enterprise meetings, Board discussions and other high-visibility business moments tied to transformation work.

- Help leaders communicate change with clarity, empathy and consistency, including when details are still evolving.

- Lead communications strategies that build employee awareness, understanding, confidence and engagement during periods of significant change.

- Design communications plans that support change readiness, adoption, feedback, leader enablement and sustained behavior change.

- Develop practical materials that help employees understand what is changing, what is not changing, what comes next and where to go for support.

- Create channels and feedback loops to surface employee questions, sentiment and areas of confusion, then adjust communications accordingly.

- Showcase progress, proof points and employee stories that make transformation work tangible and meaningful.

- Partner with transformation teams to ensure communications are integrated into program governance, planning, milestones and decision-making rhythms.

- Help identify communications risks, employee concerns, reputational considerations and stakeholder needs related to enterprise change.

- Ensure transformation messaging is clear, credible, aligned and consistent across functions, geographies and leadership levels.

- Partner with Legal, Compliance, Human Resources and other stakeholders to ensure communications are accurate, responsible and appropriate for the business context.

- Build strong partnerships across Public Affairs, HR, IT, Finance, Legal, Compliance, business functions and transformation teams.

- Coordinate with internal communications, executive communications, digital, social, brand, media and other Public Affairs partners to activate integrated plans across channels.

- Drive alignment around priorities, sequencing, messaging, stakeholder engagement and communications deliverables.

Job Description

As Director, FP&A - Global Commercial Finance & Analytics, you will play a leadership role in global commercial planning, forecasting, consolidation, reporting, controls, analytics, and finance transformation. You will serve as a trusted partner to regional and cross-functional stakeholders, translate complex financial information into executive-ready insights, and strengthen the quality, scalability, and governance of Commercial Finance processes.

Office Location: Foster City, CA

Key Responsibilities
1. Global Revenue Forecasting, Consolidation & Reporting
- Lead global commercial revenue forecasting, actuals reporting, variance analysis, and consolidated roll-ups across products and regions.

- Coordinate regional inputs and ensure consistent assumptions, standards, timelines, and quality across the worldwide forecast.

- Deliver recurring and ad hoc revenue analysis, including clear drivers, risks, opportunities, and executive-ready commentary.

- Oversee revenue-related close and planning deliverables, ensuring accuracy, completeness, and timely escalation of issues.

2. Regional Finance Partnership & Market Insights
- Serve as the primary FP&A liaison for the United States and ACE regions, strengthening alignment between regional finance teams and Global Commercial Finance.

- Partner with regional teams to understand forecast movements, business drivers, price-volume dynamics, and emerging risks and opportunities.

- Translate regional submissions into a coherent global view and provide actionable insights for leadership decisions.

3. Financial Controls, Data Integrity & Governance
- Act as a reviewer for revenue and operating expense information produced as evidence, supporting robust documentation, traceability, and control execution.

- Identify data-quality issues, investigate variances, coordinate remediation with Controllership and finance partners, and support audit-ready documentation.

- Promote disciplined financial governance, consistent definitions, and reliable reporting across systems, regions, and workstreams.

4. Cross-Functional Finance & Medical Affairs Support
- Provide finance support for Medical Affairs and other cross-functional priorities, connecting business needs with commercial financial planning and analysis.

- Serve as a liaison to PDM and G&A finance teams on cross-functional topics, including cost of goods sold and related P&L considerations.

- Coordinate inputs across Commercial, PDM, G&A, Controllership, and regional finance teams to provide an integrated financial perspective.

5. Digital Finance, AI & Analytics Leadership
- Lead Commercial Finance AI support and adoption efforts, identifying practical use cases that improve forecast quality, reporting efficiency, and decision support.

- Champion digital finance innovation, automation, self-service analytics, and standardized reporting while aligning with enterprise governance expectations.

- Develop and enhance dashboards, analytical tools, and executive reporting that simplify complex information and improve transparency.

6. Strategic Planning & Executive Support
- Support long-range planning, scenario analysis, profitability assessment, and strategic financial modeling for the global commercial organization.

- Prepare clear financial narratives and materials for senior leadership, earnings, Board, and other executive review forums.

- Provide thoughtful challenge and recommendations on investment choices, resource allocation, financial risks, and business trade-offs.

7. Leadership & Collaboration
- Operate as a trusted finance leader across Commercial, regional, corporate, and cross-functional teams.

- Influence without authority, establish clear accountability, and drive alignment across geographically dispersed stakeholders.

- Coach and develop team members, strengthen technical and business capabilities, and foster an inclusive, high-performing environment.

Basic Qualifications
BS/BA with 12+ years of relevant experience
OR
MS/MA or MBA with 10+ years of relevant experience
OR
PhD with 8+ years of relevant experience

Preferred Qualifications
- Extensive FP&A experience in revenue forecasting, financial consolidation, close, planning, and management reporting within a complex global organization.

- Demonstrated ability to partner with regional and cross-functional finance teams and translate multiple inputs into an integrated enterprise view.

- Strong knowledge of financial controls, data governance, information-produced-by-the-entity review, and audit-ready documentation.

- Advanced analytical capability, including scenario modeling, price-volume analysis, profitability assessment, and risk and opportunity evaluation.

- Experience leading digital finance, AI, automation, dashboarding, and self-service analytics initiatives.

- Executive-level communication and data storytelling skills, with the ability to convert complex analysis into clear recommendations.

- Proven change leadership, process improvement, and stakeholder management skills across virtual and geographically dispersed teams.

- Strong judgment, attention to detail, and ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.

People Leader Accountabilities
- Create Inclusion: Model inclusive leadership and embed the value of diverse perspectives in team decisions and ways of working.

- Develop Talent: Understand employees’ skills, experience, aspirations, and potential; provide coaching, feedback, and development opportunities.

- Empower Teams: Connect team goals to organizational purpose and objectives, clarify accountability, remove barriers, and enable effective collaboration across the broader ecosystem.

Job Description

MARGO Background:
The MARGO function is part of the wider Medical Affairs Research (MAR) department within the Development organization and operationalises Non Interventional Studies scientifically led from MAR. MAR conducts observational research and generates analysis results to inform decisions throughout the product lifecycle across research, development, post-approval, and commercialization. Observational research is conducted on data collected from individuals assessed for biomedical, health and other outcomes, and includes observational studies and observational analyses. Source data for observational studies may be based on primary data
collection, secondary data use, or both. The study results, generated using a rigorous process, provide insights and evidence for internal (e.g., program, safety) and external (e.g., regulators, healthcare providers) stakeholders.

Position Summary:
This role provides end-to-end operational oversight of observational studies within the MAR portfolio across all therapeutic areas (TA). This position supports the MAR team in high-quality, compliant and timely study execution of the study portfolio through effective vendor oversight, risk management and issue resolution. This role reports to the Director, MAARGO and is the primary point of contact for study operations for vendors and service providers. While not responsible for day-to-day execution, the role is responsible for collaborating with MAR scientific leads, Quality, Clinical Operations, Regulatory Affairs, Medical Affairs and other stakeholders to ensure vendors and service providers meet agreed-upon timelines and are compliant with process requirements and relevant regulatory guidelines.

Key Responsibilities:
• Responsible for working with the MARGO Leadership Team to track, prioritize and manage the execution of observational studies across all TA portfolios
• Collaborate with MARGO Leadership Team on strategic sourcing options to optimize the execution of the TA portfolio
• Responsible for vendor performance management, issue management and escalation of risks impacting the portfolio
• Responsible for the vendor oversight plans, and performance and quality checks of study deliverables per the vendor oversight process
• Partner with vendor outsourcing to support initiation and execution of study vendor and service provider agreements
• Collaborate with MAR scientific leads to ensure alignment of study objectives and timelines across all stakeholders and vendors
• Own end-to-end oversight of study deliverables, ensuring timely, high-quality completion aligned to TA priorities, with proactive risk identification and mitigation
• Track study milestones, timelines, deliverables and financials; proactively identify and mitigate risks
• Collaborate with MAR scientific leads to monitor utilization and assignment of resources to deliver on priorities established by the MARGO Leadership Team
• Ensure onboarding of study vendors and service provider resources to support the study portfolio priorities established with the MARGO Leadership Team
• Monitor end-to-end processes to ensure compliance with process requirements, regulatory guidelines and study objectives
• Serve as an escalation point to resolve quality, scope and timeliness issues with operational stakeholders, including vendors and service providers
• Maintain regular communication with operational stakeholders, study vendors and service providers to ensure delivery against priorities and commitments
• Identify opportunities for process improvement, increased standardization and operational efficiency
• Collaborate with other oversight roles within MAR to drive consistency across study execution processes and implement best practices
• Liaison with Quality on periodic quality reviews and other quality related activities
• Escalate study specific issues to Quality for guidance and consultation

Bachelor's Degree and Ten Years' Experience

OR

Masters' Degree and Eight Years' Experience

OR

PhD and Two Years' Experience

• 5+ years of experience in study operations or project management providing operational and financial oversight of observational studies
• Degree in Biology, Business, Operations Research or equivalent
• Hands-on training and experience in managing study lifecycles in GxP compliant environment
• Demonstrated experience in managing cross-functional study teams and vendor resources to balance priorities and timelines in a matrixed environment
• Proven ability to communicate the scope, requirements, expectations and standards for executing observational studies
• Proven track record of assessing vendor proposals e.g., timelines, deliverables and budget to meet study objectives
• Demonstrated vendor management experience to conduct primary data collection and secondary data use studies

Job Description

Within Global Public Affairs, the Omnichannel Strategy & Digital Transformation team owns how Gilead's reputation, innovation, and access narratives reach audiences across every channel we operate — social, paid digital, out-of-home, CRM, and the enterprise properties that support them.

The Sr. Manager, Omnichannel Corporate Engagement owns audience engagement for the Gilead public affairs across all channels. This is the person accountable for how the corporate brands show up day to day: what runs, where it runs, and how it performs.

The successful candidate writes briefs that produce good work, can tell strong agency output from adequate, produces light social assets from established brand templates, and can interpret channel performance reports to optimize outcomes.

Expertise in social media is core to this role, but media literacy beyond social is required. This role does not plan or buy media — it briefs into it, quality-controls what runs, and interprets what comes back. That requires working fluency across the paid digital channels and the corporate portfolios.

This role reports to the Sr. Director, Omnichannel Engagement.

Key Responsibilities:
Corporate channel ownership
- Own the corporate engagement plan for Gilead — content approach, publishing cadence, and channel mix — under the editorial standard set by the Sr. Director.

- Manage the corporate content calendar across owned social and engagement channels, balancing planned narrative moments against real-time opportunity.

- Translate corporate narrative and Public Affairs priorities into channel-appropriate execution, working with the internal communications, policy, and functional teams who originate the material.

- Serve as the internal subject-matter expert and day-to-day point of contact for corporate engagement across the Public Affairs function.

Agency direction and creative standard
- Write creative briefs that produce usable work, and hold the quality bar on what comes back.

- Direct agency partners across creative production and social content, managing scope, timelines, revisions, and delivery against the standard.

- Produce light social assets in-house using established brand templates where speed or volume makes agency routing impractical.

Paid media support and channel literacy
- Brief creative into paid campaigns for the corporate portfolios, coordinating execution with the media discipline owner and agency partners.

- Quality-control creative and placements before they run, including brand safety, adjacency, and format compliance.

- Interpret cross-channel performance and feed insight back into the next flight.

- Work within the media standards, audience targeting approach, and budget allocation set by the media discipline owner. Direct the work; do not own the buy.

Working fluency is expected in the channels the corporate portfolios rely on most:
- Paid social: Meta, LinkedIn, X, YouTube, TikTok, Reddit — objectives, placements, and creative specs.

- Paid search: Google Ads and Microsoft Advertising — brand-term and keyword campaigns, and how paid interacts with organic and AI-generated search results.

- Programmatic display, native, and video: how inventory is bought through a DSP, the difference between open exchange and private marketplace deals, and what viewability and brand-safety controls do.

- Measurement vocabulary: impressions, reach and frequency, CPM, CTR, video completion rate, viewability, share of voice, and sentiment — enough to read an agency report critically and ask the right questions of it.

Social listening
- Manage the social listening program day to day — directing the monitoring agency, maintaining the queries and competitor set, and running the reporting cadence.

- Translate listening insight into content opportunity and competitive context for the corporate portfolios.

- Surface emerging reputational risks promptly on the established escalation path to Public Affairs leadership and Corporate Communications.

Measurement and reporting
- Own corporate channel performance — engagement, reach, share of voice, sentiment, completion — and report against the enterprise measurement framework.

- Use performance data to adjust content mix, cadence, and creative approach.

Bachelor's Degree and Eight Years' Experience
OR
Masters' Degree and Six Years' Experience

Preferred Qualifications

- 5+ years in corporate social, digital communications, or content and channel management, ideally within regulated, reputation-sensitive, or enterprise environments.

- Demonstrated ownership of a corporate or brand channel end to end — plan, calendar, execution, and performance — not solely campaign support.

- Working knowledge of paid media mechanics beyond social, sufficient to brief, quality-control, and interpret agency-led campaigns across the channels listed above. Hands-on buying experience is not required; the ability to hold an agency to account is.

- Strong editorial and creative judgment, with the ability to set and hold a standard on agency output.
- Background in public affairs, corporate communications, or reputation management, either in-house or agency-side.

- Practical production capability with brand templates and platform-native formats; working fluency in Adobe Creative Suite or equivalent for light asset creation.

- Experience with enterprise social publishing and listening platforms (e.g. Sprinklr, Sprout Social, Brandwatch, Talkwalker), and the judgment to distinguish noise from an emerging issue.

- Comfort with web and campaign analytics (e.g. GA4, platform-native reporting) and the measurement vocabulary above.

- Proven comfort operating inside Legal, Medical, and Regulatory review and governance workflows, with content that consistently clears compliance.

- Excellent collaboration and stakeholder-management skills in a matrixed, cross-functional organization, including comfort advising senior leaders.
- Experience in pharmaceutical, biotech, or another regulated industry.

- Familiarity with policy, health-trade, or advocacy media environments.

This role serves as the enterprise integrator for the HIV Treatment business, partnering closely with Brand Leadership, Sales, Medical Affairs, Market Access, Insights & Analytics, Finance, Commercial Operations, and Global teams to identify portfolio opportunities, establish strategic priorities, guide investment and resource allocation decisions, and enable coordinated decision-making across brands. The role is accountable for portfolio direction, governance, prioritization, and strategic integration, while brand and capability leaders translate those priorities into specialized strategies, activation plans, and business outcomes.

The Senior Director identifies and frames the portfolio's most consequential strategic choices, evaluates opportunities, risks, dependencies, and trade-offs across brands, and develops objective recommendations that enable timely executive decisions and coordinated organizational action. This includes assessing growth opportunities, competitive responses, investment trade-offs, and future priorities.

Key Responsibilities

The Senior Director, Portfolio Strategy is accountable for defining the integrated HIV Treatment portfolio strategy, establishing portfolio priorities, leading cross-brand decision-making, and optimizing investment and resource allocation across the business.

The role does not own brand, customer engagement, media, digital, field, or channel strategies. Instead, it establishes the portfolio direction, priorities, governance, and decision frameworks that guide those functions. Brand teams and portfolio capability leaders translate portfolio priorities into specialized strategies, execution plans, and measurable business outcomes.

Portfolio Strategy, Growth & Investment Prioritization
- Lead the development and alignment of the integrated HIV Treatment Portfolio Strategy, defining the role of each brand and how brands work together to address evolving patient, customer, and market needs.
- Own the portfolio planning framework, connecting long-range strategy, annual planning, investment decisions, and business reviews into a cohesive roadmap.
- Assess market dynamics, competitive trends, customer needs, policy developments, and emerging innovations to identify the growth opportunities, risks, and strategic choices most critical to the future performance of the HIV Treatment portfolio.
- Develop recommendations on portfolio positioning, competitive responses, future growth opportunities, and strategic priorities to strengthen long-term franchise performance and competitiveness.
- Establish governance, prioritization, and decision-making processes that support effective resource allocation and resolution of cross-brand trade-offs.
- Lead portfolio investment planning and performance reviews, recommending where resources should be increased, sustained, redirected, or reduced to maximize portfolio value.
- Champion a portfolio-first mindset that balances individual brand objectives with broader franchise priorities, long-term growth, and patient impact.

Commercial Alignment & Operating Model
- Translate portfolio strategy into enterprise priorities, strategic guardrails, and operating principles that guide how brands work together across the HIV Treatment portfolio.

- Define governance structures, decision rights, prioritization frameworks, and planning processes that enable effective coordination across brands and functions.

- Establish portfolio priorities and strategic guardrails that brand and capability leaders use to shape customer engagement, field, digital, media, Next Best Action, and other specialized strategies.
- Ensure commercial investments are evaluated based on both brand impact and contribution to overall portfolio objectives.
- Drive alignment across cross-functional stakeholders when strategic trade-offs, competing priorities, or resource allocation decisions require enterprise-level decision making.

Leadership & Strategic Influence
- Align senior leaders around portfolio priorities, strategic choices, and investment decisions.
- Translate market, customer, competitive, and financial insights into clear recommendations and decision-ready options for leadership.
- Champion high-priority cross-functional initiatives requiring coordination across commercial, medical, market access, analytics, operations, and global teams.
- Bring external perspectives, emerging trends, and evolving customer needs into portfolio planning and decision-making.
- Serve as a trusted strategic advisor to senior leadership on portfolio growth, competitiveness, and long-term value creation.

Measures of Success
- Leadership has a clear and aligned view of portfolio priorities, strategic choices, investment needs, and the role of each brand.
- Portfolio, brand, and functional plans are connected through effective governance, coordinated decision-making, and transparent resource allocation.
- Cross-brand synergies are maximized while brand differentiation, accountability, and strategic focus are preserved.
- Portfolio resources and investments are focused on the highest-value growth opportunities and strategic priorities.
- Portfolio priorities are consistently translated into aligned strategies, coordinated execution, and sustainable franchise growth.

- Investment and resource allocation decisions consistently improve portfolio performance, strategic focus, and long-term franchise value.

Job Description

The Director, Sales Leader Development & Commercial Operations Capabilities will lead two distinct areas within Global Commercial Learning & Development: sales leader development, with an initial primary focus on the U.S., and a global Commercial Operations competency model. Reporting to the Senior Director, GCLD, this role will translate business priorities and role expectations into practical, scalable solutions that improve performance and support long-term talent development.

The Director's primary focus will be leading and sustaining the U.S. Regional Director New-to-Role Learning Journey and development for tenured sales leaders, with the flexibility to support broader regional and affiliate needs over time. Globally, the Director will build a Commercial Operations competency model that defines skills, behaviors, proficiency expectations, and development priorities across global and affiliate teams. The role will partner with GCLD, Global Commercial Excellence, Commercial Operations Directors, U.S. CL&D, U.S. sales leaders, HR/Talent, and regional and affiliate teams.

The successful candidate will combine commercial and field acumen with learning strategy expertise and the ability to lead complex work across a matrixed organization. They will align senior stakeholders, turn business needs into clear solutions, manage multiple workstreams, and measure learning and commercial impact. This role will sit in Foster City, CA.

Key Responsibilities:

Sales Leader Development
Primary focus is supporting the execution, sustainment, and continuous improvement of U.S. sales leader development, aligned to business priorities and field needs.
Own the Regional Director New-to-Role Learning Journey, including curriculum planning, stakeholder alignment, delivery, reinforcement, evaluation, and improvement.
Own and evolve leadership development for tenured sales leaders, including the Content Guide and other governed resources that support consistent application.
Apply adult learning principles and field experience to create practical, application-based learning, tools, and resources.
Support additional sales leader development priorities across regions and affiliates as business needs evolve.

Global Commercial Operations Competency Model
- Lead the design of a global Commercial Operations competency model that defines competencies, behaviors, and proficiency expectations across global and affiliate roles.
- Partner with affiliate stakeholders, Commercial Operations Directors, HR/Talent, GCLD, GCE, and subject matter experts to validate role requirements and align the model with job architecture and talent processes.

- Supports regulatory filings and inspections.

Senior Manager, Global Clinical Supply Chain is a leader that who carries out leadership vision and directions while providing expertise for Gilead's global clinical trials. Works collaboratively within the department and with cross functional colleagues (e.g., Regulatory, Clinical Operations, Quality, PDM Product Strategy teams, GSC, Information Technology, etc.) to develop strategies, meet project deliverables, and solve business problems. - Keeps abreast of clinical supply incidents and issues. Reports and escalates issues as well as investigates root cause as appropriate.
- Performs tasks in Gilead systems (e.g., SAP, IVRS, QMS, etc.) to enable compliant and efficient progression of IMP through the supply chain.
- Authors SOPs and business process work instructions as per leadership direction and support.
- Supports regulatory filings and inspections.
- Maintains compliance of clinical supply deliverables for clinical study reports (CSR) and trial master file (TMF).
- Maintains compliance with required training.

- Bachelor’s degree with 8+ years of industry experience OR Master’s degree with 6+ years of experience OR PhD or PharmD degree with 2+ years of experience.
- Degrees in the sciences preferred.
- Strong working knowledge in clinical supply management including and not limited to forecasting, demand / supply planning, IVRS and ERP systems.
- Strong working knowledge of clinical study designs, blinding practices, global trials, from Phase 1 first in human to late phase.
- Strong working knowledge of Clinical Demand and Operations Planning (CD&OP).
- Experience with managing comparator drugs and other co-meds for clinical studies.
- Ability to collaborate, influence and negotiate to work effectively with cross-functional teams and external suppliers to meet clinical development timelines and patient needs.
- Works effectively with ambiguity. Ability to devise, assess and implement best options in alignment with Gilead's core values and functional expectations.
- Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills. Ability to write clear and concise documents/presentations.
- Strategic, enterprise thinking with ability to distill complex business problems to technology solutions.
- Strong or excellent computer skills (e.g., email, word processing, spreadsheet creation and management, online search, etc.). Ability to efficiently adopt systems and databases used at Gilead.

Job Description

Job Description:
- As the External Manufacturing Scheduler at Kite, you are responsible for building and maintaining executable production schedules across our external manufacturing (CDMO/CMO) network. You act as the primary planning conduit between Kite Network Planning, Site Supply Chain and our external partners, translating demand plans into contractually-aligned external forecasts, securing plasmid, vector and other critical material availability, managing purchase orders and invoicing, and governing schedule performance. This role ensures that external partner capacity, slot reservations, material readiness and release convert into stable, reliable supply across all external manufacturing nodes.

Responsibilities :

External Production and Release Scheduling
- - Own, build, and maintain the production schedule across all external manufacturing nodes, maintaining synchronized calendars with partners for end-to-end visibility.
- Validate slot reservations, campaign timing, yield expectations, testing sequences, and release timelines with external partners.
- Protect schedule stability within the frozen window while enabling agility in the longer horizon. Manage exceptions through established supply governance forums and provide partners with rolling 6–24 month visibility to enable proactive contracting, capacity planning, and risk mitigation.
- Reconcile forecasted demand against contracted capacity, escalating gaps or over-commitments for resolution.

Plasmid & Critical Material Management
- - Own forward CMO planning for plasmid and Cell Banks confirming supplier feasibility and readiness ahead of scheduled campaigns.
- Partner with Procurement, Materials, and External Quality to align material availability, safety stock, and procurement strategies with the schedule.
- Proactively identify material constraints and drive mitigation to prevent disruption.

Purchase Order & Invoicing Management
- - Issue and manage POs to external partners in alignment with the schedule, forecast, and contract terms, tracking status through the full lifecycle to closure.
- Manage invoicing with partners, including validation, reconciliation against POs/deliveries, and resolution of discrepancies.
- Partner with Finance, Procurement, and Accounts Payable for timely financial processing, budgeting, accruals, and spend visibility.

Performance Management & Reporting
- - Track, analyze, and report KPIs across the external network: schedule adherence, capacity utilization, supply reliability/OTIF, forecast accuracy, inventory health, and PO/invoicing accuracy.
- Partner with Quality to capture deviations, understand root-cause drivers, and drive corrective actions with partners.
- Ensure adherence to plan stability metrics, managing exceptions through established governance processes.

External Tools & Maintenance to Support Daily Operations
- - Partner with system/IT teams to establish and maintain robust, efficient systems, tools, and data structures for managing external information.
- Establish standardized reporting, dashboards, and data flows for accurate, timely visibility across the network.
- Lead continuous improvement initiatives to strengthen planning discipline, reduce cycle time, and improve integration.

Cross-Functional & Partner Coordination
- - Serve as the central scheduling interface between Kite and the External Manufacturing organization and external partners.
- Coordinate shipments with internal sites, logistics and trade compliance to assure timely supply across Kite’s network.
- Lead recurring scheduling forums with External Manufacturing, Quality, Regulatory, Technical Operations, and Supply Chain to align on feasibility, constraints, and assumptions.
- Assure variation management is aligned with external manufacturing schedule including part number management

Qualifications
- - Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Operations, Engineering, Life Sciences, or related field with relevant experience; OR Master’s degree with correspondingly less experience; OR PhD with correspondingly less experience.
- Supply chain planning experience with strong exposure to external manufacturing (CDMO/CMO) and network/site planning.
- Deep understanding of GMP operations, external manufacturing, batch-based production, and global distribution flows.
- Experience translating demand plans into supplier forecasts and managing supply within contractual frameworks.
- Experience issuing and managing purchase orders and invoicing with external partners.
- Proficiency with ERP and advanced planning systems (SAP, IBP, OMP, Kinaxis).
- Strong influencing skills across global, matrixed organizations and external partners.

Preferred
- - APICS CPIM/CSCP certification or MBA (advanced degree).
- Experience with cell & gene therapy, commercial biologics, or sterile injectables.
- Experience with plasmid / critical raw material planning.
- Experience with S&OP/S&OE processes and supply governance frameworks.

Key Capabilities
- - Strong ability to translate strategy and demand into executable external production plans.
- Excellent communication, alignment, and stakeholder engagement skills across internal teams and external partners.
- Highly analytical with advanced scenario planning capability.
- Effective at navigating complex external networks, contracts, and competing priorities.
- Calm, structured, and decisive during supply escalations.
